reading.body:
A data center entry in Deer Valley, Arizona could not be confirmed as an operating facility, and its coordinates resolve to an unrelated garage-door company.

The record carries no operator, no website, no power figure, and no business registration. The coordinates at 33.6647455, -112.1117142 reverse-geocode to A1 Garage Door Service on West Behrend Drive in Phoenix, roughly 17 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor. The name Accelera Data Systems is generic enough that it does not by itself imply colocation or hosting. The most likely explanations are a stale or imprecise OpenStreetMap pin, or an address vacated since it was tagged.

This matters for AI infrastructure accounting because a facility with no published capacity cannot be counted toward the power that constrains compute. Arizona has four facilities with published power figures totaling 512 MW. This site contributes zero megawatts to that total, not because it is small, but because nothing about it is verified. Treating unconfirmed entries as real would inflate the state's apparent capacity, and treating them as absent would understate it if the facility exists under another name.

What the data does not establish is whether any data center ever operated here. It also does not connect this address to the other eight rows in its batch, which sit 15 to 20 miles away with no shared building. The entry is filed as unconfirmed, and that is the whole of what can be said.
